newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 fabricated aluminium demand seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 fabricated aluminium demand seen flat.

text.p: Demand for Japanese aluminium mill products was forecast at 2,500,400 tonnes in the fiscal year beginning April 1, virtually flat from 2,500,340 tonnes in 1996/97, the Japan Aluminum Federation said on Thursday.

The federation predicted a slump in demand from the construction sector, after a strong performance in 1996/97 fuelled in part by a rush to purchase homes ahead of April's national sales tax increase.
This would be offset, however, by continued but slower growth in demand from the beverage can and automobile sectors.

Despite stagnant demand for beverages overall and competition in the soft drink market from the 500 ml PET bottle, the federation said aluminium cans' market share in beer packaging would continue growing while the weakening yen would limit any threat from imports.
In the automobile sector as well, although car output was expected to be flat in the next fiscal year, aluminium use in car radiators was likely to continue expanding at copper's expense.
